Rule: All three visible cells contain an identical black square; the fourth cell must match this constant shape to complete the pattern.
Every cell contains the same figure, so the missing cell must show a plus inside a circle as in the other three cells.
Each row mirrors horizontally: the second image is the left-right reflection of the first, so the missing cell is the mirror of C (identical to B).
Shape rotates 90° clockwise across the row and 90° counter-clockwise down the column, giving the same orientation as cell A.

Each column keeps the same shape (triangles in column 1, squares in column 2) while moving from the top row to the bottom row flips the figure vertically; therefore B’s bottom-left black square becomes a top-left black square in the missing cell.

The second column repeats the diagonal of the first column but fills the triangle on the same side of that diagonal with black, while the second row flips the diagonal direction of the first row; therefore the missing cell must have the flipped (\) diagonal of C with the corresponding half shaded black.
Each entry in the right-hand column is the corresponding entry in the left-hand column rotated 90° clockwise; therefore the answer is C rotated 90° clockwise.
Each row keeps the same black-white arrangement while the shape changes from circle on the left to square on the right, so the missing cell is a square with white left and black right halves.
Rows keep the same shape while changing from outline to filled across columns; columns keep the same fill style while changing shape down rows, so the missing cell must be a filled square.

Going right, the inner circle is removed and a hollow square is added; going down, a filled square is added. Combining both operations gives one circle enclosing a hollow square enclosing a filled square.

Rows keep the same outer shape (top: hearts, bottom: octagons) while columns control the presence of the inner diamond (left column: diamond present, right column: diamond absent), so the missing bottom-right cell must be an octagon without a diamond.
The number of concentric circles is reduced by two each time you move right or down in the matrix, so the missing cell must contain just one circle.
The number of concentric squares increases by one as you move down each row and across each column, so the missing cell must contain three nested squares.

The outline square increases one size step with every move rightward and with every move downward, so the bottom-right cell needs the next larger single outline square containing the same central filled square.
The number of diamonds in a cell equals (row number) × (column number), so the bottom-right cell needs 3 × 3 = 9 diamonds.
Moving right adds one circle to the horizontal row while moving down adds one circle to the vertical stack (forming rectangular grids), so the bottom-right cell must be a 3×3 grid of 9 circles.
Each move to the right or downward adds one extra surrounding dot so counts increase by one in every row and column; therefore the bottom-right cell must show the star with five dots.
Width increases from left→right and height increases from top→bottom, so the bottom-right cell must have both maximum width and maximum height – a large square.

The circle’s position in each cell is the combination of its row (top, middle, bottom) and column (left, centre, right) coordinates, while the diamond always stays in the centre; the missing bottom-right cell therefore needs a centre diamond with the circle in the bottom-right corner.

Within each column the total number of squares stays the same while, moving downward, two more squares change from filled to outlined; thus column-3 goes from 0→2→4 outlined squares, so the missing cell must contain four outlined squares.

Within every column the figure in the 2nd row is made by duplicating the 1st-row figure vertically so that the copies touch, and the 3rd-row figure is made by duplicating them again but leaving a gap; applying this to column 3 requires two vertically separated copies of C placed side-by-side, i.e. four non-touching diamonds.

In every row the number of vertical diamonds equals 3-rowIndex and stays constant, while each step to the right adds one new diamond to the bottom row; thus the third column needs 3 bottom-row diamonds with no extra vertical ones.
In every row the third panel shows the union of the white squares that appear in the first two panels, so combining G and H must give the plus-shaped five-square figure, which is option 6.

Each row shows the same shape repeated, while each column must contain one star, one heart and one octagon, so the blank (row 3, column 3) must be the same outlined octagon as the other two in its row.
The three filled shapes (circle, diamond, triangle) form a 3×3 Latin square so each shape appears exactly once in every row and column, so the missing cell must be the filled circle.

Each row and column contains one panel with 1 shape (a circle), one with 2 shapes (triangle+circle) and one with 3 shapes (triangle+circle+square); the missing panel must be the remaining 1-shape circle.

Rows keep the same inner symbol (row 1 plus, row 2 star, row 3 heart) while columns keep the same outer border (column 1 circle, column 2 diamond, column 3 square); thus the missing cell is a heart inside a square.

In every row: cell 1 has a polygon inside a big circle, cell 2 swaps them (circle inside polygon), cell 3 keeps the polygon and replaces the big circle with two small outer circles; the polygon changes by row (square, diamond, octagon), so the missing cell is an octagon with two small circles.

Each row has 3, 2, then 1 concentric squares while the three inner symbols (circle, plus, triangle) form a Latin square so every row and column contains each symbol exactly once; thus the bottom-right cell must be the circle inside a single square.

Each row and column must use every centre shape (plus, square, heart) and every surround type (dots, circle outline, same-shape outline) exactly once; the empty cell therefore needs the only unused combination: a solid square with surrounding dots.

Each row contains the three shapes square, diamond, circle in cyclic order, and each column cycles the fill style filled → composite → outline; the third-row, third-column cell must therefore be a filled diamond.

Each row and each column must contain every outer shape (circle, octagon, square) and every stripe type (vertical, horizontal, cross) exactly once; the missing combination for column 3 / row 3 is an octagon with a vertical stripe.

Both across rows and down columns the central shape cycles square→diamond→circle while the type of arms cycles small squares→diagonal lines→cardinal lines; the missing cell must be the next in both cycles – a square with diagonal arms.
Each row (and column) contains the three star styles exactly once, cycling rightward each row; the third row needs the solid star to complete the cycle.

Shapes cycle squares→triangles→stars while the quantities 3,4,5 also cycle, so each row and column contains exactly one 3-shape, one 4-shape and one 5-shape; the blank must be the missing 3-triangle cell.

In every row the third panel shows the union of all the shapes that appear in the first two panels of that row, so combining G (left+up) and H (right+down) must give a figure containing left, right, up and down triangles.

The figure in each cell is the union (superimposed overlay) of the two figures directly above it and/or to its left; therefore the missing figure must overlay all the parts present in C (plus+square) and F (circle+X).
In every row and column the third cell is the pixel-wise XOR (symmetric difference) of the first two; G XOR H leaves only the outer square.

In every row and every column the centre cell is exactly the union of the shapes contained in the two outer cells, so the missing cell must supply just the diamond (and dot) that, together with G, gives H and, together with C, gives F.

In every row and column three visual elements are present pair-wise: each cell shows exactly two of them and each element must appear exactly twice across the three cells, so the blank must contain the two elements (plus sign and corner squares) that are still missing a second occurrence in its column.
In each column the bottom cell is the symmetric-difference (XOR) of the two cells above it; C ⊕ F gives a square outline with both diagonals.
In every row the right-hand cell repeats the top shape of the left cell and the bottom shape of the middle cell, so ? needs the top of G (outline triangle) and the bottom of H (filled square).

In every row and in every column the third figure shows only those arrow-like protrusions that appear on BOTH of the first two figures (set intersection of directions Up, Down, Left, Right); thus the bottom-right cell, common to Up∩Down = ∅, contains just the central square with no protrusion.
The third row is a horizontal mirror of the first row (cells in Row 3 replicate Row 1 in reverse order), so the missing cell must match Cell A (three upright triangles).
Across the row the triangle is rotated 90° clockwise, while down the column the figure is replicated three times, so the missing cell is three right-pointing triangles in the rotated arrangement.
Each cell is a 180° rotation of the cell that is diagonally opposite it; therefore the bottom-right cell is A rotated 180°, i.e. a downward-pointing isosceles triangle.

Row-wise the regions between successive outlines are coloured alternately black and white starting with black at the outside, while column-wise the lower figure has two fewer nested squares than the upper; applying both to C gives outer black ring / white gap / inner black ring / white centre.

Left-to-right the pattern alternates colour: starting from the second ring, every other space is filled solid black, while top-to-bottom the two outermost rings are removed (5 rings become 3), so the bottom-right cell must be the 3-ring figure whose middle ring is filled.
Each row and each column loses one of the shapes as you move right or down (2→1→0 shapes), so the bottom-right cell must contain no shape at all.

Going across each row, the solid-black triangle in the first cell changes to the same-shaped hatched triangle in the second; going down each column, the black/hatched region moves to the opposite side of the same diagonal, so the missing cell must be the hatched version of C.
Shape is mirrored left–right across each row and mirrored top–bottom (while changing from solid to striped) down each column, so the answer is the striped circle with its top-left quarter missing.
Number of polygon sides increases by 1 across each row and by 2 down each column, so the missing figure must have 6 sides (a hexagon).
Left-hand column shows striped shapes, right-hand column shows the same shapes completely filled, so the striped heart must become a solid heart.

Across each row the figure is mirrored left-to-right, and down each column it is mirrored top-to-bottom, so the missing cell must be B flipped vertically / C flipped horizontally: arrow head on the left, along the bottom edge.

The figure in each row is the left-hand figure rotated 90° clockwise, and the figure in each column is the top figure with five extra sides; applying both to the bottom-right cell gives a rotated octagon (visually identical to the octagon in C).

The pattern in the grid moves one step down-and-right: every cell (except those in the first row or column) is an exact copy of the cell that is one position up-and-left of it, so the bottom-right cell must be identical to the centre cell E.
The count of squares increases by exactly one as you move right or down, so the bottom-right cell must contain five squares in a horizontal row.

Each cell forms a rectangular grid whose number of columns equals the column index (1,2,3) and whose number of rows equals the row index (1,2,3); cells with an even (row+column) sum are hollow, odd are filled, so the missing cell must be a 3×3 grid of 9 hollow triangles.

Across each row the number of horizontal lines increases 1→2→3, while down each column the number of vertical lines increases 1→2→3, so the missing cell must contain 3 vertical and 3 horizontal lines.

The grid is numeric: moving one step right or one step down always removes one item (4−(row+column)); cells whose row+column is even show circles, odd show squares, so the (2,2) cell must contain 0 items – i.e. be blank.

In each column the shape type is fixed (triangles, circles, squares) and the number of shapes increases by +1, +2, +3 down the rows respectively while the fill alternates solid/outline each row; thus the bottom-right cell must show 9 outline squares.
The number of triangles equals (row index × column index) and orientation is down when row+column is even and up when it is odd, so cell (3,3) needs 3×3 = 9 downward triangles.
Across every row and down every column one texture is gradually replaced by the next (Black → Stripes → Dots: 0 %, 50 %, 100 %), so the bottom-right cell must be 100 % dots.

In every row the small copy of the shape moves from outside (1st column) to partly overlapping (2nd) to completely centred inside the large copy (3rd); the missing cell must therefore show a small diamond centred inside a large diamond with the dot in its centre, which is option 7.

Each row uses one shape family (row1 circles, row2 squares, row3 octagons) and moves left-to-right from two separate outlines with a central dot, to the two outlines partially overlapping, to two concentric outlines containing a filled centre; therefore the missing cell must be concentric octagons with a central filled octagon.
Each row multiplies the number of shapes in the first row by the row index (1,2,3) while each column keeps the same shape; thus the bottom-right cell must contain 3×3 = 9 squares.

Each row and each column contains the three shapes (triangle, circle, square) and the three sizes (small, medium, large) exactly once in a cyclic Latin-square pattern; the bottom-right cell must therefore be the medium-sized circle.

In every column, the bottom-left quadrant is added when moving from the second to the third row, so the last cell is cell F (top half black) plus the bottom-left quadrant, leaving only the bottom-right quadrant white.
Moving one cell to the right or one cell down, the mouth of the Pac-Man shape is rotated 90° clockwise, so the missing cell must have the mouth pointing right like in cell A.
Row 3 is Row 1 rotated 180°, so the triangle that corresponds to the upward-pointing triangle in A must be the downward-pointing isosceles triangle.

Border style changes down each column from dashed to solid to double, while the three inner symbols cycle across each row (star → propeller → diamond), so the missing cell must have a double border and a propeller inside.
Each row and each column must contain one star, one heart, and one octagon, and also one outline, one striped, and one solid fill; the missing cell must therefore be the striped star.

Each row and each column contains every background (white, striped, dotted) and every bar shape (vertical, horizontal, cross) exactly once; the missing cell must therefore pair the only background and bar type not yet used in its row/column: white background with a cross.

Within every row, the three-triangle outline in the third column is the same orientation as the filled triangle in the first column and is positioned opposite the direction it points; since the filled triangle in the last row points down, the answer must be three outline triangles pointing down with two at the top and one beneath.

Rows are cyclic shifts of the sequence 2-, 3-, 4-edged figures (row1: 2-3-4, row2: 3-4-2, so row3 must be 4-2-3) and every row/column contains exactly one curved side; the required cell is therefore a 3-edged figure with one curved side.
The quantity of symbols cycles 2→3→4 across each row, shifting one column to the right on the next row, so the last cell must contain exactly 2 symbols.

In every row and every column the third cell contains only the shapes that appear in BOTH of the previous two cells (set intersection); applying this to row 3 / column 3 leaves only a single triangle.

In each row, the left-hand figure is the union (overlay) of the two figures to its right, so the shape that must combine with the blank square H to give the striped rectangle G is a vertical-striped rectangle alone.
Each move right or down adds two sides to the regular polygon (4,6,8 / 6,8,10 / 8,10,12), so the missing cell must be a 12-sided polygon.
The shape gains two points as you move one step right or one step down, so the bottom-right cell must be the 12-point star.

Each row contains the same three shape types in the order (polygon, many-point starburst, 4-point star) but the first two swap places every row; the 4-point star is always in the third column, so the missing cell is another 4-point star.

Within the 3×3 grid each successive cell (left-to-right, top-to-bottom) adds the next item of a fixed nine-position sequence, so cells contain 1,2,3 … up to 9 shapes; the missing cell must therefore show all nine shapes (the previous eight plus a circle in the bottom-right corner).
Number of birds increases by one as you move right across each row and also increases by one as you move down each column, so the bottom-right cell must contain 5 birds.
